notes: CIRCUIT: a three-rail ladder/mesh. Top rail y~348 (x 158..908) is broken in the middle by the 15MF cap #0; middle rail y~512 (x 89..982) is broken by the 9MF cap #8 and the 4MH inductor #7; bottom rail y~678 (x 157..900) is broken by the 1MH inductor #17. Four vertical columns (x~360, 546, 738, 906) each carry one diode/zener from the top rail to the middle rail and another from the middle rail to the bottom rail. The 8V/1kHz V-AC #6 sits between the top rail (through the 5MH inductor #1) and the middle rail; the 3A I-DC #15 sits between the middle rail and the bottom rail (through the 1MF cap #18). The left end of the middle rail ends in the sideways GND #9; its right end goes through resistor #10 down to GND #16. NET MAP: n1 = top rail LEFT of the 15MF cap: right end of L1 (5MH), top of zener #5, top of diode #4, left plate of C0. n2 = top rail RIGHT of the 15MF cap: right plate of C0, top of zener #3 (744,373), top of diode #2. n3 = top of the V-AC #6 and the left end of L1. n5 = middle rail CENTRE section (x 425..761), between the 9MF cap and the 4MH inductor: left plate of C8, bottom of diode #4, top of zener #12, bottom of zener #3, top of diode #14, left end of L7. n4 = middle rail RIGHT section (x 856..982): right end of L7, bottom of diode #2, top of diode #11, top of resistor #10. n7 = bottom rail LEFT of the 1MH inductor: right plate of C18, bottom of diode #13, bottom of zener #12, left end of L17. n6 = bottom rail RIGHT of the 1MH inductor: right end of L17, bottom of diode #14, bottom of diode #11. n8 = bottom of the I-DC #15 and the left plate of C18. '0' = ground: the middle rail LEFT section (x 89..425) with GND #9 at its left end, the bottom of the V-AC #6, the top of the I-DC #15, the bottom of zener #5, the top of diode #13 and the right plate of C8; plus the bottom of resistor #10 into GND #16 (a second GND symbol, same node by convention). SITES: eleven sites recorded, all junctions. S1 (546,350), S2 (361,356), S0 (744,345) are T's where a column lead lands on the top rail; S35 (738,676), S37 (354,678), S39 (544,680) are T's where a column lead lands on the bottom rail. In each of those the column ink terminates at the rail, so a crossing reading would leave that diode/zener lead dangling. (S0 is only load-bearing after the port fix on zener #3 below, which is why the tracer did not flag it CRITICAL; it is recorded here because it now carries zener #3's top terminal onto n2.) The five four-way sites S15 (546,512), S16 (733,511), S17 (359,512), S18 (103,516) and S19 (906,514) are where a column crosses the middle rail. I dumped the pixels at S15 and S18 with inkmap: both are plain X's - two ~3 px strokes crossing, no solder blob (the crossing patch is no fatter than the strokes) and no hop or sideways jog; nothing anywhere on this sheet is drawn with a hop, so by the ink prior a plain crossing here means connected. Electrical check confirms it for four of them: reading S15/S16/S17/S19 as crossings would each split off a two-terminal island made of the column's upper and lower devices in series (diode #4+zener #12, zener #3+diode #14, zener #5+diode #13, diode #2+diode #11 respectively) with no return path to anything - an impossible reading. S18 is the one where both readings are electrically survivable (the V-AC and the I-DC would end up in series between the top and bottom rails, with the middle rail passing behind them); I read it as a junction because (a) its ink is identical to the other four crossings on the same rail, which must be junctions, (b) the drafter never draws hops on this sheet, and (c) it puts the return of both sources on the grounded middle rail, which is the sane physical reading. The consequence of the other reading would be: V-AC bottom + I-DC top become their own two-terminal net and the ground rail no longer references either source. Non-critical sites (S5, S6, S8, S9, S10, S11, S21-S31, S34, S40-S42) are all handwritten value text ('5MH', '9MF', '4MH', '1MH', '8V 1kHz', '3A') or symbol ink brushing a wire; S34 (140,592) is the '3A' label touching the current-source circle and its tracer default (crossing) is harmless. PORT FIXES: three components had a terminal parked on a stroke of the handwritten value label instead of on the real lead - each showed up as a one-terminal net. Zener #3: t1 was on the '5 V' text at (790,422); the real top lead is port p1 at (744,373) running up to the top rail right section, so t1 -> p1 (net n2). Capacitor #8 (9MF): t1 was on the '9MF' text at (461,539); the real left lead is port p1 at (425,509) with a 63 px wire running left to the middle-rail left section, so t1 -> p1 (net 0). Zener #12: t1 was on the '5 V' text at (587,584); the real top lead is port p2 at (546,535) running up to the middle rail centre, so t1 -> p2 (net n5). No class looks wrong: #3, #5, #12 are drawn with the bent zener cathode bar, #2, #4, #11, #13, #14 are plain diodes, and the sideways symbol at (55,516) really is a GND (three shrinking bars) rather than a capacitor. UNRESOLVED: none.
